title: Greedy Best-First in Porto: the fastest-looking path!
description: Watch Greedy Best-First race across a real street-map graph, always choosing the next node that looks closest to the goal. It’s fast and intuitive—until the city reveals a detour trap.
ig_caption:
🌉 Porto streets, 🧭 one goal: reach the destination fast with **Greedy Best-First**! 

🔎 **What Greedy Best-First does (in this visualization):** it treats the map as a graph (intersections = nodes, roads = edges) and uses a heuristic function **h(n)** (e.g., straight-line distance to the target) to pick the next node that *seems* best. 

⚡ Each step expands the node with the lowest **h(n)** in a priority queue—so it can feel “laser-focused” and move quickly toward the goal. But because it ignores the full path cost (no true g(n) accumulation like A*), it may chase a promising shortcut and get stuck near misleading neighborhoods 🧩—a classic tradeoff in heuristic search. 

🗺️ Real-world twist: the street layout + river-side geography means the heuristic can be optimistic when barriers/turn costs exist, turning the shortest-looking route into a lesson about graph search behavior. 

👉 Want to see how changing the heuristic reshapes the route? Comment **“HEURISTIC”** and follow for more real-map algorithm drops!
fb_caption:
Can an algorithm “feel” its way to the goal? In this Greedy Best-First visualization, Porto’s streets are modeled as a graph (nodes/intersections + edges/road segments), and the algorithm repeatedly selects the next intersection with the smallest heuristic distance to the destination. 

✅ Fast, goal-directed search—but it can still take a suboptimal route when the heuristic is misleading. Share this with a friend who loves mapping + computer science and tell us: should we compare it next to Dijkstra or A*?
yt_description:
Porto (Ribeira) street map visualization using **Greedy Best-First** pathfinding! In this YouTube Shorts clip, we model the city as a graph (intersections/nodes + roads/edges) and run Greedy Best-First, selecting the next node by the lowest heuristic distance to the goal. 

🎯 Keywords: greedy best first search, pathfinding visualization, real map algorithms, heuristic search, graph theory, shortest path, coding reel, priority queue. 

Watch the route update step-by-step and learn why it’s quick but can be misled by “looks-close” heuristics. Try it with different heuristics in your own code—then comment what you notice!
